questions.prompt: After Chapter 14 diagnoses inertia and entropy, what does Chapter 15 add?
choices: How the book's ideas work together as one strategic discipline
How to choose one favorite concept and ignore the rest
How summary alone creates strategy
questions.explanation: Chapter 15 is about synthesis: connecting the book's ideas into one reinforcing chain of diagnosis and action.

questions.prompt: What does synthesis mean in this chapter?
choices: Reciting the major ideas in order
Linking diagnosis, action, force, timing, and structure into one method
Choosing whichever concept sounds strongest in the moment
questions.explanation: Putting it together is more than summary. It means using the parts as one coherent discipline.

questions.prompt: Which mistake does the chapter criticize?
choices: Testing whether the strategic links reinforce one another
Treating one good concept as enough without the rest of the chain
Connecting structural diagnosis to coherent action
questions.explanation: The chapter warns that isolated insight is weaker than disciplined synthesis.

questions.prompt: A school plan uses strategic words confidently, but diagnosis never connects to action and timing never connects to structure. What is the Chapter 15 diagnosis?
choices: The plan is integrated because it sounds intelligent
The plan is fragmented rather than truly synthesized
The plan only needs more slogans
questions.explanation: A plan is not synthesized just because it borrows the language. The reinforcing chain has to be present.

questions.prompt: Why do diagnosis and coherent action belong together?
choices: Because strategy weakens when analysis and action split apart
Because diagnosis should stay separate from design
Because action matters only after growth decisions
questions.explanation: Diagnosis without action stays descriptive, and action without diagnosis becomes forceful confusion.

choices: By ignoring structural realism and focusing only on goals
By turning structural diagnosis into integrated strategic practice
By treating drag and decay as unrelated to action
questions.explanation: Chapter 14 diagnosed resistance and decay; Chapter 15 shows how that diagnosis has to be joined to the full strategic chain.

questions.prompt: A side project improves only after diagnosis, focus, timing, and structure are aligned. What concept is this showing?
choices: Strategic synthesis
Proof that one strong concept was enough
Evidence that diagnosis can be ignored
questions.explanation: The project gets stronger because multiple strategic links are reinforcing one another as one discipline.

questions.prompt: What is the best sign that a plan is fragmented rather than integrated?
choices: Its major concepts sound good but do not clearly reinforce one another
Its diagnosis leads directly to coherent action
Its timing and structure are aligned with its force
questions.explanation: Fragmentation appears when the plan borrows ideas without connecting them into one working chain.

questions.prompt: Why is isolated insight weaker than disciplined synthesis?
choices: Because one concept cannot replace the reinforcing strategic chain
Because every concept should be used separately
Because summary is stronger than application
questions.explanation: The chapter argues that a single concept is not enough when diagnosis, force, timing, and structure all affect whether the strategy holds.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter point toward strategist mindset?
choices: Because once the method is integrated, the next question is what judgment can use it well
Because the final chapter abandons the earlier concepts
Because integration makes judgment unnecessary
questions.explanation: Chapter 15 builds the integrated method so the final chapter can ask what kind of thinker can actually practice it under pressure.
